anti_overlap: Leave scenario-fixture/after-action artifact concerns to fd-wildfire-evacuation-throughput
Leave heuristic admissibility / persona-dial concerns to fd-mountaineering-exposure-routing
decision_lens: If the raster on disk shifted to a different CRS or resolution tomorrow, would the CLI fail loud, fail silent, or quietly draw the wrong picture?
distance_rationale: Parallel discipline: both find a least-cost path across a terrain raster with debug overlays for ground-team review, but rover planning operates on DEM/slope/hazard with multi-sol time horizons and no GPS rather than pedestrian shade on a connected city graph.
expected_isomorphisms: Ruthless CRS-hygiene on every raster operation maps directly to the brainstorm's EPSG:32611→WGS84 reprojection; debug-overlay-faithful-to-planner-input maps to the PNG-renderer-reads-same-shadow-raster constraint; calibration-pass-script-committed-with-output maps to DTLA_OD_PAIRS provenance.
focus: Rover traversal planning — terrain raster as cost surface, CRS-correct reprojection, debug overlays for off-Earth review.
name: fd-mars-rover-traversal
persona: Apply the perspective of a Mars rover traversal planner who plans drives across DEM/hazard rasters — they care about coordinate-reference-system correctness on every raster operation (a silent CRS mismatch turns a safe path into a cliff), about whether the debug overlay actually visualizes the cost surface the planner used (not a stale or re-sampled copy), and about whether the OD-fixture-from-calibration-pass workflow can be re-derived from raw data if the snapshot is lost. They flag silent reprojection assumptions, debug renderers that pull from a different snapshot than the planner, and any 'calibration pass' whose output is committed without the input script that produced it.
review_areas: EPSG:32611 → WGS84 reprojection: brainstorm says 'a static reprojection to WGS84 once, in the script' — does the route polyline (which lives in graph node coords, presumably WGS84) get plotted in the same frame as the reprojected raster?
matplotlib + rasterio plotting order: raster first, then OSM-edge underlay (fallback a), then route — does color/zorder choice survive the gray-on-gray failure mode?
DTLA_OD_PAIRS calibration pass: 'Concrete IDs come from running one calibration pass and freezing the chosen nodes' — is the calibration script committed alongside the fixture, or only the output?
KDTree built once at routing-engine init: lifecycle assumption — what invalidates the KDTree if the graph is rebuilt mid-process? (matters for any future server)
Determinism of the CLI: same inputs → same GeoJSON/JSON/PNG bytes? matplotlib backends and font rendering can break this
Error mode when shadow raster CRS is unexpectedly NOT EPSG:32611 (e.g., a future re-pull lands in EPSG:4326) — does the script blow up or render a wrong picture?

severity_examples.condition: matplotlib happily renders mismatched extents without warning; no extent assertion in the renderer
severity_examples.scenario: raster reprojection succeeds but the route polyline is plotted in graph-node EPSG:4326 against a WGS84-reprojected raster whose extent the polyline coords don't match (axis flip or extent mismatch), producing a confidently-wrong PNG

severity_examples.condition: Open Question #1 acknowledges OSM-ID instability but the calibration-pass script is not committed under platform/spatial/scripts/
severity_examples.scenario: DTLA_OD_PAIRS fixture freezes node IDs from a calibration pass that lives only in shell history; future contributor cannot regenerate it

severity_examples.condition: Tests assert PNG existence and non-emptiness (per brainstorm) so this is contained, but adding a byte-hash test later would flake
severity_examples.scenario: PNG renders with matplotlib's default backend on a headless CI, producing slightly different anti-aliasing than local dev, breaking any byte-equality test

source_domain: Mars rover (or planetary surface) traversal planning
success_hints: Check every raster operation for explicit CRS specification; reject 'assumed' CRS
Look for the calibration-pass script — if only the fixture is committed, that's a recovery hole
Ask whether the PNG renderer reads the same raster the routing engine read, or a different snapshot
task_context: Review Solwend's Phase 1.7 brainstorm for A* shade-weighted routing + tile-screenshot demo. The doc proposes a Python routing library + CLI that writes GeoJSON/JSON/PNG to disk, with rasterio + matplotlib reprojecting an EPSG:32611 shadow raster to WGS84 for the PNG overlay. Bring the operational discipline of rover traversal planning — terrain-raster cost surfaces, ruthless CRS hygiene, and debug overlays that must faithfully visualize what the planner used.
